tests/test_serve_edit_keyless_handle.py:.requirement: Control: the list route hands the keyless row its ~<relpath>:<line> handle and the read route answers it; handle minting is unchanged by this task.
POST /api/item/<~handle>/edit saves the yaml-list-item (200 applied, lands in the item's own span, no key minted); base answers 422 'in this file'.
The same save through the keyless handle of a md-front-matter item (items/notes.md) succeeds and leaves the body prose standing.

Saving through the keyless handle is identical to saving through the display id: same bytes, same patch describe, same new revision, same response shape; each response reports what the read route reports for its own ref.
The handle's line is validated, not guessed: a handle whose line no longer points at the item's definition (file shifted on disk) refuses and writes nothing.
A hand-built handle naming a real file and a line that is no item's definition is the ordinary refusal, with the tree byte-identical.
The handle's file is part of its identity: REQ-002's reqs.yaml line number spelled against notes.md (where no item is defined) refuses and writes nothing.
Control: the display-id handle keeps saving on the keyless project.
Control: the surrogate-key handle keeps saving on the keyed project (EDIT-01 behavior stands).

A stale-revision save through the keyless handle is the 409 with a real diff (current_text + diff, like the display-id save); base strips the conflict of its text because the plan cannot use the raw ~ spelling.
